1How many signatures get notarized?
$15 each · the most Colorado law allows

Every signature gets its own stamp. Two people signing one document = 2.

2Where do we meet?

Miles are counted round trip (there and back) from 5128 E Colfax Ave, Denver, CO 80220, my office at Tienda Salvadoreña.

    To count the miles, what you type goes to komoot’s OpenStreetMap address search (for the suggestions) and, if you don’t pick one, to the U.S. Census Bureau’s free address lookup. The map points go to OpenStreetMap’s route service. I don’t save your address. Data © OpenStreetMap contributors.

    Example: if you’re 15 miles from the store, that’s 30 miles round trip, so pick “A bit farther.” Travel is charged once per visit. Not sure? Pick your best guess and I’ll confirm it.

    What I do

    • Notarizations$15 a signature

      Affidavits, powers of attorney, vehicle titles, travel consent for kids. You bring the document filled out, not signed.

    • At the airport (DIA)$95 + $10 a signature

      Flying out and just found something unsigned? I’ll meet you in the terminal before security. Parking’s on me.

    • Certified translationsfrom $30 / page

      Spanish to English, done by me, with my signed certification. I prepare them to meet USCIS requirements; the agency decides.

    • Colorado apostillesfrom $85

      Document going to another country? I walk it into the Secretary of State’s office in Denver and bring it back to you.

    • Certified copies$15 / copy

      Diplomas, passports, IDs. I need to see the original. Colorado birth and marriage records come from the county or state, not me.

    • Loan signings & I-9sfor businesses

      I print the loan package and meet the borrowers; I don’t prepare or explain the documents. I-9 Section 2 as your authorized representative.

    How it goes

    1. You text me

      What the document is, how many people are signing, and what city you’re in.

    2. I send the total

      One price with travel included, plus a time. Nothing’s booked until you say yes.

    3. We sign

      I check each person’s ID, you sign in front of me, and I stamp it.

    Have ready

    • The document, unsigned.
    • A government ID for each signer, current or expired less than a year.
    • Everyone who’s signing, in the room.

    I’m the one who shows up, not an employee or someone I send. Spanish and English are both my native languages, I studied at MSU Denver, and I’ve spent more than 5 years helping people with their paperwork. If there’s something I can’t do, I’ll tell you up front.

    — David · more about me

    Meet me on Colfax and skip the travel fee

    $10 a signature and no travel fee at my office inside Tienda Salvadoreña (5128 E Colfax Ave), the Auraria Library at MSU Denver, or any Denver Public Library branch. Still by appointment: I’m out on visits most of the day, so text me before you come.

    Getting to my office

    1. Park in the shared lot behind the building.
    2. Walk around the side to the sidewalk on Colfax.
    3. Go in the front door of Tienda Salvadoreña.
    4. My office is on your left.

    Open in Google Maps · The other spots

    The Auraria Library and Denver libraries are public places where I meet clients by appointment. I’m not affiliated with, sponsored by, or endorsed by any of these locations.

    What people usually ask
